narration: Black Friday: checkout traffic triples. Pay for idle servers all year, or scramble on the day? This is KubeSage: an AI SRE team for Kubernetes, built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon.

FinOps and SRE, in one system. It plans savings, forecasts rushes from usage and your calendar, and fixes what breaks. Small models do the legwork, so runs cost cents. Every finding must cite evidence. Agent fixes are git commits. And plans and fixes reach the cluster only when a person applies them.

Meet shop-prod: a hypothetical store on Azure Kubernetes. Five services share one node, at two hundred eighty dollars a month. Two reserve two cores each, and sit mostly idle. Checkout peaks every weekday morning. Black Friday is on the calendar. And tonight, a ledger cache ships with too little memory.

So FinOps and engineering keep one business calendar: working hours, Black Friday, Christmas week. KubeSage reads it with thirty days of usage, and forecasts each rush with no model call: when to pre-warm, and how many pods. A flash sale nobody planned? A CPU trigger catches it. And for Black Friday, the plan asks for a one-day scale-up from seven thirty.

Statistics and the forecast are free. One Muse Spark call triages every workload. Spark handles the routine fixes; Muse Wonder takes the hard case and the node pool. Guardrails floor requests from history and restore dropped calendar pre-warms. Total: twenty-seven cents, under half the price of all on Wonder.

When an alert fires, four small agents gather evidence in parallel. A finding with no collected signal? Dropped. A larger Thinker reads the rest, plus your team's plain-English rules, and finds the root cause. The Executor writes the fix as a git commit, after policy checks limit each edit.

Here's the simulated cluster. Each glass is the CPU a pod reserves. Hit Analyze: seventy percent less reservation cost, for twenty-seven cents. The forecast shows each service's biggest rush, with its pre-warm time and pods. And to fit scheduled peaks, the node pool costs thirty-two percent more.
Apply right-sizes the services and adds the KEDA rules. It skips moving pods until the new nodes exist.
Then, the bad release: ledger-cache runs out of memory, and the ContainerOOMKilled alert fires.
The team jumps in on its own. Sub-agents report, the Thinker finds the cause, and the chat shows every hand-off.
The fix is a commit: more memory, a memory-optimised node pool proposal, and two security fixes. Sixteen seconds. Two cents. A person decides.
That's KubeSage: FinOps and SRE in one system, built on Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, with a person in charge.
